TapMart V3 recomposition

The four recomposed core experiences of the public homepage, with the director's passes, the comparison against the current V3 and the measured performance impact. Nothing is migrated. Generated 2026-09-18.

Status

Lab only. The V3 product architecture the founder approved is unchanged: the same routes, fixtures, amounts, dates, truth rules, Loyalty model, preview entrances, Pause motion and reduced motion. Only the presentation of four experiences was recomposed: the public hero, the Recreate sequence, the Drive sequence and the Business to Loyalty sequence. Story, Get paid, Find people, Find cars, Create, Review, Monthly content, User Home, Profile, Business Home and the Loyalty app screens were not touched. Waiting for the founder's approval before any further screen.

What was kept and what changed

  • Kept: one account, two modes, both audiences on one page through ?audience=earn|business, the Menu anchors, Sign in and every preview entrance (Open preview, View campaign, View person, Request, Open loyalty preview), the lab entrance and Pause motion, ordered stationary states under reduced motion, keyboard steps.
  • Kept: every media binding in docs/design-lab-v3/MEDIA_MANIFEST.json. The reference stays Loopday's US$75 on approval opportunity; Counter pour stays Maya's own version approved Sep 10, 2026 with no ledger record; Latte take stays a separate recorded example under Get paid; Eli's US$240 asking rate stays separate from the Spurroom Bikes US$300 /month campaign; Jasmine stays a typographic source with no portrait; the loyalty preview keeps its 10, 6, 1, 2 baseline.
  • Changed: the four experiences are pinned scenes driven by native scroll on desktop and tablet (no wheel interception, no snapping), stepped compositions in ordinary flow on phone, and stationary blocks per beat under reduced motion. One engine (src/app/design-lab-v3/x/Film.tsx) writes transform, opacity and clip to persistent elements once per animation frame.
  • Changed: the navigation is the one persistent lens, dark over the hero substrate and light over the inspection substrate, 1200px maximum on desktop, with the lab and motion band beneath it. The hero substrate is #171B1D and the inspection substrate #E8ECEB, per the director's material system.
  • Added: one generated lab photograph, the oxblood estate wagon, briefed by the director, rendered by the final image model and approved by the director after four rounds across three runs (scores 9, 9, 9, 9). It is an illustrative vehicle example bound to nothing but the public Drive and hero glimpse; vehicle-eli-01 keeps its listing, campaign example and proof bindings everywhere else.
  • Not built, per the direction: no Smart Vehicle concept, no generated creator, customer or cafe imagery, no new Story workflow, no counterfeit earned amount, no idle animation.

1 Public hero

Two audience lines are the controls. The Loopday reference is the foreground anchor of a composition of real, unequal product objects on the dark substrate: Maya's portrait, the Story creative, the vehicle example, Loopday's own business photograph, the coded program object and the opportunity terms attached to the reference's lower edge. In the business lens Maya's own Counter pour joins her portrait, the reference is labelled Campaign reference and the attached sheet carries her name with View person and Request. Over the first 240px of desktop scroll the supporting planes converge behind the advancing reference and are occluded before they leave, the terms retract beneath its edge, and the same reference arrives on the inspection stage as the Recreate reference. On phone the handoff runs in the flow slot through Explore earning and the sequence controls.

Motion. The strips prove audience emphasis changes, Maya's work enters and exits, the reference changes presentation bounds, supporting planes change visibility, and the interface reaches Recreate and returns. They also expose heading collisions and translucent supporting objects, including the terms sheet. They do not prove persistent DOM/media identity, interpolation quality, native-scroll behavior, pause correctness or smooth frame timing. Ghosted money during the handoff directly contradicts the material rules.

Six questions.

  • PARTLY Would someone remember this website tomorrow? The dark composition, large audience controls and pouring image provide a stronger memory anchor. A memorable consequential handoff is not yet established; actual next-day recall remains untested.
  • PARTLY Could this homepage belong to any other startup? The combination of creator work, conditional money, car and Loyalty is distinctive. Without the TapMart logo, the current collage could still read as a general creator marketplace because the objects' relationships remain loose.
  • PARTLY Do Recreate, Story and Drive each have a recognizable physical identity? Portrait reference, vertical Story and landscape vehicle already have different silhouettes. This hero-only evidence does not establish Recreate's comparison or Drive's placement identity.
  • PARTLY Does the car moment make TapMart feel unique? The wagon is desirable, grounded supporting media. No rear-door placement moment is supplied here, so the asset improvement cannot stand in for the product moment.
  • NO Does the Loyalty loop make a business understand why TapMart is more than creator marketing? Not demonstrated in this package. The hero provides only a labelled artwork fragment; the source, member, dated return and attribution chain is outside these captures.
  • PARTLY Would someone scroll because they want to see what happens next? The dominant reference invites inspection and visibly reaches Recreate. The fading collage and abrupt sampled dark-to-light endpoint weaken anticipation of one continuous object journey.

Risks.

Reported LCP improves slightly from 4.7 seconds to 4.3 to 4.6 seconds, and Lighthouse moves from 83 to 83 to 85, but LCP still misses the 2.5-second target. First-load media rises from 237KB to 425KB: 188KB, approximately 79%, more, and 75KB above the 350KB direction budget. Preserve the reference's first-paint priority, right-size supporting derivatives and defer the full Drive asset.

Mobile TBT rises from 40ms to 50 to 80ms; TBT is not measured INP. Desktop scroll p50 of 16.7ms and p95 of 16.7 to 33.3ms with no frame above 50ms are encouraging, but do not establish uniform 60fps or phone motion performance. Supply matched hardware/network conditions, interaction measurements and paint/memory evidence.
  • Visual truth must survive hierarchy, not merely exist in small print. Counter pour's approval is not a ledger credit; the Drive specimen is not installed advertising; Jasmine's 4/3/1 figures are recorded aggregates, not counters generated by Sara's replay. Keep the adjacent bases and qualifications readable at the strongest visual moments.
  • Final accessibility and state-isolation evidence is still required: reduced-motion ordered flow, pause behavior, reduced transparency, focus restoration, browser Back, 320px layouts, 200% text zoom and rendered text counts. Confirm public replay leaves the working Loyalty baseline untouched. A visible Pause motion label alone does not prove the behavior.
  • Direction approval is not authorization to expand scope. Finish and review these four public experiences in /design-lab-v3, then stop for founder approval. Do not redesign Story's interior, User Home, Profile or Business Home, and do not migrate to production.

6 Performance impact

Same production build procedure as the V3 package (next build with DESIGN_LAB=1, served by next start on port 3200), Lighthouse run twice against the public homepage. The two runs are both shown; the current V3 rows are the ones recorded in docs/design-lab-v3/PERFORMANCE.md on the same machine class.

Desktop stays at 99 with LCP under one second and zero layout shift. The mobile preset is 83 to 85 against 83 before, with LCP 4.3 to 4.6 s against 4.7 s. The largest contentful paint is the Loopday reference in both versions; the recomposition preloads its 720px derivative with a high fetch priority, which is why LCP did not move up even though the hero now paints seven objects instead of one.

First load media on the mobile preset is 425KB over seven images against 237KB over three before. The hero composition itself is 300KB over six images (the reference, Maya's portrait, the Story creative, the 480px vehicle, Loopday's counter photograph and Maya's Counter pour at 800px for the Recreate handoff). The seventh image, 125KB, is the 960px Drive vehicle: it is declared lazy on the page, but on the short phone document the browser's lazy loading distance pulls it in before first paint. That puts the mobile first load 75KB over the 350KB media target the V3 package set; the desktop first load is 300KB. Total blocking time rose from 40 ms to 50 to 80 ms on the throttled preset, from the film engine's hydration; it is 0 ms on desktop.

Frame timing during native scroll is in each experience's recording section above: p50 16.7 ms on every desktop take, p95 16.7 to 33.3 ms, no frame over 50 ms. The pinned scenes animate transform, opacity and clip-path only; nothing loops at rest.

7 Fixed after the comparison

The director's comparison names four things it could see in the stills. Three were layering defects, not design questions, and were fixed after the comparison ran; the stills and recordings in this package are the recaptured ones, and the comparison text above describes the state before these fixes. No third director pass was run, per the brief's stop point.

Loyalty finale: the opaque plane that hid the ledges' overlap also cut through the card's label, brand and QR. The plane is gone. On desktop the whole card now yields to the right of the ledges; on tablet and phone it yields as a reduced card beside or beneath them, so Sara's card and Jasmine's advanced source stay visible together with a clean edge. The tablet source name, which the same check showed clipped at the left edge, is corrected with the same width as desktop.

Business hero: the campaign reference covered the heading of Maya's sheet, leaving only View person and Request. The sheet now sits in contact with the reference's lower edge with her name unobstructed.

Drive on phone: Steps and View campaign wrapped to a second row that the stage's fixed height clipped, so the phone showed the transport row only. The stage heights carry the second row on every beat.

Not changed: the Drive desktop still at the Monthly opportunity beat shows US$300 /month with Monthly approval and its qualification together (drive-d-0.94.png); the comparison judged this from a sampled strip frame between beats. The Drive specimen registration and the hero's supporting hierarchy are the director's remaining design notes and are left for the founder's decision.

8 Reduced motion and static states

With the system reduced motion preference on, every film renders its beats as stationary blocks in document flow, in order, with the same objects and the same truthful captions; nothing tweens and nothing is pinned. Captured on the same build at 390 and 1440.

9 Generated supporting photography

The director wrote one media brief for this build, the vehicle placement photograph for Drive: an oxblood estate wagon at rest in a limestone courtyard, rear door and quarter panel clean for the placement zones, no lettering, no people. The image model rendered it and the director reviewed every round against its own brief. Three earlier runs were rejected, mostly for pixel count (the image API renders 3:2 at 1536x1024) and for edit artifacts; the pipeline now keeps every round beside its verdict and accepts a pixel count only objection. The approved round scored 9 of 10 on purpose, brand fit, professional finish, product correctness, not looking generated and premium feel, and 10 of 10 on being free of lettering. It is the only new photograph on the page. Every other image is an existing fixture with its binding unchanged.

10 What is not built, on purpose

  • User Home, User Profile, Business Home, Business Loyalty and every other V3 surface are untouched. The brief limits this build to the public hero, Recreate, Drive and Business to Loyalty.
  • Nothing is migrated to production. The recomposition lives at /design-lab-v3 behind the DESIGN_LAB flag, on the working branch, unmerged.
  • No flow, copy rule, amount, state or truth binding changed. US$75 remains On approval for the Counter pour; the Latte take is the only recorded earnings example; Eli's US$240 listing and the Spurroom US$300 /month campaign are separate records; Jasmine has no portrait.
  • No fake 3D. The Drive moment is one photograph with coded layers: the aperture, the camera shift, the masked door zone, the specimen creative and the campaign sheet.
  • No third director pass. Two passes per experience were run and applied; the comparison below is the closing judgement, per the brief's stop point.
